stories.title: Anthropic researcher resigns and warns about self-improving AI
stories.summary:
Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned over extinction-risk concerns and has become a prominent AI-doomer voice.

- Warns about self-improving AI and calls for pacing agreements between leading labs
- Describes a "mini Manhattan project" inside Anthropic and says it's "crunch time for humanity"
- Argues AI labs have only a few years left to make their systems safe, and that alignment remains unsolved
- Anthropic's own alignment lead co-signed his warning rather than walking it back
- His account has gone viral, with coverage of the controversy reportedly reaching 133 million views
- Now on a media tour discussing his warnings across multiple outlets; the timing coincides with Anthropic reportedly preparing for an IPO

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, its first "critical" cyber-capability model
stories.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, a computer-use/agentic model that leadership framed as marking the start of an "AGI era." It's the first OpenAI model to cross the company's Preparedness Framework "critical" cybersecurity threshold — scoring 100% on ExploitBench and finding real zero-days in testing — so its most advanced cyber capabilities are initially limited to trusted defenders via Daybreak Blue. OpenAI committed $1 billion under "Daybreak for Frontline Defenders" to expand access to that frontier cyber AI, plus training and support, for essential services. Astra posts strong benchmark results, though OpenAI's framing has drawn scrutiny over what those numbers measure and the absence of its GDPval real-world-work benchmark. It is rolling out to enterprise, ChatGPT and API customers with tiered pricing and additional monitoring safeguards; early access problems left some paying users unable to use the new model, prompting Sam Altman to apologize and offer usage resets. A separate critique argues that Astra's more advanced, less legible reasoning makes the human oversight OpenAI has championed harder to provide.

stories.title: Meta debuts Muse, a personal AI agent powered by its Spark model platform
stories.summary: Meta has introduced Muse, a personal AI agent that can carry out online tasks such as shopping, travel booking and selling a car. It is built around Meta’s Muse Spark model platform, whose 1.3 release improved coding and long-running agent performance; its strongest configuration remains in limited preview and a promised open-weight release is delayed. Muse’s requested access to email, calendars, payments and health services makes privacy and user trust central to Meta’s consumer AI bet, while the company is also offering Spark users a discount in exchange for usage data.

stories.title: Apple's fall event pushes AI further into iPhone, Watch, and Siri
stories.summary:
Apple's fall event put AI at the center of its lineup, drawing both interest and unease.

- Apple Watch and iPhone gain "Audio Intelligence" features that transcribe and summarize nearby conversations, which Apple says won't save raw audio but critics warn normalizes always-listening devices
- iOS 27 brings a fully revamped Siri assistant, positioned as Apple's most substantial AI overhaul yet
- New CEO John Ternus argued the iPhone itself is already users' "personal AI device," signaling Apple is talking about AI more directly than before
- Commentary is split: some frame Apple's low-key approach as a refreshing contrast to rivals' AGI ambitions, while others (CNET) urge people to just talk to each other instead of relying on Audio Intelligence
